title: Zeniff Among the Lamanites
summary: Zeniff recounts being sent to spy among the Lamanites. After seeing good among them, he desired that they not be destroyed.

explicit_facts.text: Zeniff had been taught in the language of the Nephites and knew the land of Nephi, also called the land of their fathers’ first inheritance.
Zeniff was sent to spy on the Lamanites’ forces so that his army could attack and destroy them.
After seeing good among the Lamanites, Zeniff desired that they not be destroyed.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Zeniff is among Lamanites while spying.
unspecified_visual_details: The clothing, ages, and physical features of Zeniff and the Lamanites.
The exact place and circumstances of Zeniff’s observation.

narration.text: I, Zeniff, having been taught in all the language of the Nephites
I was desirous that they should not be destroyed.

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the intended attack as occurring.
Do not identify the Lamanites present as warriors or invent what good Zeniff saw.

title: The Dispute and Return
summary: Zeniff contends for a treaty; the ruler orders him slain, but fighting within the army leaves many dead. The survivors return to Zarahemla.

explicit_facts.text: Zeniff contended with his brethren in the wilderness because he wanted their ruler to make a treaty with the Lamanites.
The ruler was austere and bloodthirsty and commanded that Zeniff be slain; Zeniff was rescued amid much bloodshed.
The army fought internally, father against father and brother against brother, until most of it was destroyed.
The survivors returned to the land of Zarahemla to tell their wives and children what had happened.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The dispute and internal fighting occur in the wilderness.
unspecified_visual_details: The ruler's identity, appearance, and exact role in the fighting.
How Zeniff was rescued and the precise circumstances of the internal combat.
The route and duration of the return to Zarahemla.

narration.text: I contended with my brethren in the wilderness
father fought against father, and brother against brother
we returned, those of us that were spared, to the land of Zarahemla

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the ruler's name or depict the wives and children as present during the return.

title: A Second Journey
summary: Zeniff gathers those willing to possess the land of their fathers and leads them into the wilderness, where they suffer famine and afflictions.

explicit_facts.text: Zeniff gathered as many as desired to go up and possess the land of their fathers and began another journey into the wilderness.
The group suffered famine and afflictions and were slow to remember the Lord their God.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Zeniff and his people travel together through the wilderness.
unspecified_visual_details: The size and composition of the traveling group.

narration.text: collected as many as were desirous to go up to possess the land
we were smitten with famine and sore afflictions

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a particular divine cause or miracle; the verse gives no visible event of that kind.

characters: Unnamed group who pitched the tents
locations: The place where their brethren were slain, near the land of their fathers

title: Zeniff Goes to the King
summary: Zeniff enters the city with four men to learn the king's disposition and ask to settle peacefully. The king covenants that Zeniff may possess Lehi-Nephi and Shilom.

explicit_facts.text: Zeniff went into the city with four men and approached the king to learn his disposition and whether he could enter with his people and possess the land in peace.
The king covenanted that Zeniff might possess the land of Lehi-Nephi and the land of Shilom.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Zeniff and his four men are before the king in the city.
unspecified_visual_details: The king's court, architecture, clothing, and appearance.

he covenanted with me that I might possess the land of Lehi-Nephi, and the land of Shilom.

title: The King's Design

characters: The group described as “they” in verse 12
locations: The land yielded by King Laman

explicit_facts.text: King Laman yielded land intending to bring the narrator's people into bondage.
After the narrator's people had dwelt in the land for twelve years, King Laman grew uneasy that they might become too strong to overpower and bring into bondage.
The group described as “they” desired to bring the narrator's people into bondage for their labor and flocks.

title: The Attack South of Shilom
summary: In Zeniff's thirteenth year, while his people water and feed flocks and till their lands south of Shilom, a large Lamanite force attacks, killing people and taking flocks and corn.
locations: south of the land of Shilom

explicit_facts.text: In the thirteenth year of Zeniff's reign, his people were watering and feeding flocks and tilling lands south of Shilom.
